## Part 2 — Configuration Architecture

| Dimension | What it controls | Levels | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Depth** | How deeply the skill is tailored to the buyer's domain | Generic / Vertical-tuned / Fully-custom-forked | Fully-custom-forked requires Commercial or White-label license |
| **Breadth** | How many offerings/verticals one buyer can run it on | Single-offering / Single-vertical / Unlimited | Unlimited blocked at Generic depth (no value-add) |
| **Support** | Human backup behind the skill | Self-serve / Async-SLA / Live-debug / Operator-on-call | Operator-on-call requires Vertical-tuned or higher |
| **Memory** | Persistence and learning across runs | None / claude-mem default / Custom backend with dashboard | Custom backend requires Async-SLA or higher |
| **Output** | Where the blueprint lands | Markdown only / +JSON-YAML / +Direct push to configurator tools | Direct push requires Vertical-tuned |
| **License** | Distribution rights | MIT (open) / Commercial single-seat / White-label | White-label requires Fully-custom-forked depth |
| **Certification** *(domain-specific)* | Operator credentialing for consultants who resell productization to *their* clients | None / Listed operator / Certified-with-badge-and-leads | Certified requires Live-debug support or higher |
| **Eval Rigor** *(domain-specific)* | Run-quality guarantee | None / Self-test harness / Maintainer-reviewed run audits | Audits require Async-SLA or higher |

**Invalid combinations the configurator must block:**
- Unlimited breadth + Generic depth (no reason to pay for unlimited if not tuned)
- Fully-custom-forked depth + MIT license (forked work returns to commercial terms)
- Operator-on-call + Generic depth (operator needs vertical context)
- Direct-push output + Markdown-only (contradiction)
- White-label + None memory (white-labeled product without persistence is brittle)
- Certified operator + Self-serve support (can't certify without live touchpoints)

## Part 3 — Three Tiers + Build-Your-Own

Naming in the skill's own vocabulary: **Clay / Studio / Foundry**.

### Tier 1 — **Clay** (Lite)

- **Configuration:** Generic depth · Single-offering breadth · Self-serve support · No memory · Markdown output · MIT license · No certification · No eval rigor
- **Positioning:** For the solo consultant who wants to productize *their own* offering once, using the public skill as-is.
- **Pricing logic:** **Free / MIT.** This is the funnel and the credibility anchor — the open-source skill must remain genuinely useful standalone, or the paid tiers look extractive. Anchor: the cost of *not* productizing (one lost custom engagement worth +$X).

### Tier 2 — **Studio** (Core, flagship)

- **Configuration:** Vertical-tuned depth · Single-vertical breadth · Async-SLA support · claude-mem default memory · Markdown + JSON/YAML output · Commercial single-seat license · Listed operator · Self-test harness
- **Positioning:** For the agency, coaching practice, or consulting firm running the skill across their full book — tuned to their vertical, with memory that compounds across client runs and an SLA when it breaks.
- **Pricing logic:** **+$B/year subscription.** Anchored against (a) one prevented mis-scoped engagement per year, and (b) the cost of an internal ops person building a configurator from scratch (~3–6 months FTE). Must price *below* the sum of BYO equivalents (Vertical-tune + SLA + memory + commercial license summed à la carte) so flagship remains the rational choice.

### Tier 3 — **Foundry** (Premium)

- **Configuration:** Fully-custom-forked depth · Unlimited breadth · Live-debug + Operator-on-call support · Custom memory backend with dashboard · Direct-push output to buyer's configurator stack · White-label license · Certified-with-badge-and-leads · Maintainer-reviewed run audits
- **Positioning:** For the productization consultancy, larger agency, or platform that wants to *embed* Intelligent Clay into their own offering — white-labeled, custom-forked, with the maintainer effectively as a fractional partner.
- **Pricing logic:** **+$C/year** (substantially above Studio — typically 4–8×). Anchored against a fractional senior consultant's retainer + a custom-built internal tool, summed. Below the cost of building and maintaining the equivalent in-house (~$250–400K loaded eng-year).

### Build-Your-Own Framework

- **Base price:** Clay (free, MIT) + per-dimension upgrade pricing à la carte
- **Per-dimension upgrade pricing (placeholder tokens — re-anchor once you set Studio's $):**
  - Depth: Generic → Vertical-tuned (+$D1) → Fully-custom-forked (+$D2)
  - Breadth: Single-offering → Single-vertical (+$Br1) → Unlimited (+$Br2)
  - Support: Self-serve → Async-SLA (+$S1) → Live-debug (+$S2) → Operator-on-call (+$S3)
  - Memory: None → claude-mem (+$M1) → Custom backend (+$M2)
  - Output: Markdown → +JSON/YAML (+$O1) → Direct-push (+$O2)
  - License: MIT → Commercial (+$L1) → White-label (+$L2)
  - Certification: None → Listed (+$C1) → Certified (+$C2)
  - Eval Rigor: None → Self-test (+$E1) → Audits (+$E2)
- **Floor:** Clay (free) — anything paid starts at Vertical-tuned depth OR Async-SLA support, otherwise the buyer should stay on the free tier
- **Ceiling:** Any config combining 4+ premium-level dimensions auto-routes to Foundry (or to a custom quote)
- **Configurator must enforce:** all dependencies and invalid combinations listed in Part 2
- **Flagship-protection rule:** The à-la-carte sum to reach Studio's exact configuration must price **above** Studio's flat annual price. Same for Foundry. Concretely: `D1 + Br1 + S1 + M1 + O1 + L1 + C1 + E1 > Studio price`. If you ever set per-dimension prices that violate this, Studio loses its anchor and rational buyers atomize instead of buying the bundle.
